title: Streamlined artifact attestation and graceful profile rollout orchestration
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Build an end-to-end CI/CD flow that produces deterministic model artifacts, attaches cryptographic attestations, and performs staged performance-profile promotions without requiring manual gating. This ticket covers the orchestration glue (pipeline templates, policy engine hooks, and rollout controller) and the artifact-side contract (signed provenance envelope + metadata schema).

Scope and deliverables:
- Deterministic build step that records build inputs (git sha, model weights checksum, toolchain versions) and outputs a canonical artifact tarball.
- Attestation envelope: adopt a small SLSA-inspired JSON envelope signed by KMS (customer or Redwood HSM) containing oracle checksums, quantization metadata, and perf-profile pointers.
- CI templates: GitHub Actions & internal runner templates that produce signed artifacts and publish to the internal model registry.
- Rollout controller: a service which consumes profile metadata and can perform staged promotions by percent, region, and customer tier. Support canary percentages, time windows, and automatic rollback triggers based on quality and latency signals.
- Audit + verification: post-publish verification step that validates signatures, checksums, and a smoke-runner that executes a small suite of perf/quality traces against the published profile.
- Operational dashboards and alerts: surface promotion progress, signature failures, and canary health (P90 latency, token cost delta, eval accuracy drift).

Design trade-offs considered:
- Option A: enforce strict attestation (blocking) before publish. Pros: safety. Cons: increases time-to-publish and requires broader infra changes to KMS.
- Option B (chosen): non-blocking attestation pipeline that marks artifacts as "provisionally published" until attestation completes; provisional artifacts are not auto-pinned for customer-facing routes. This keeps onboarding fast while retaining verifiable provenance.

Acceptance criteria:
- CI produces an artifact tarball + attestation envelope for 95% of test model commits without manual intervention.
- Attestation signature verified by registry and visible in artifact metadata UI.
- Rollout controller can perform a 5% -> 25% -> 100% promotion with automatic rollback on defined SLO breaches.
- Logs and dashboards show per-step provenance and publish durations.

Implementation notes:
- Use existing signing library (pkg/signing) and integrate with KMS adapter (kms-adapter). For now call Redwood KMS; add feature flag for customer-managed KMS later.
- Reuse model-registry artifact schema but extend with "attestation_v1" field and "provisional" boolean.
- Rollout controller will be implemented as part of infra/services/release-orchestrator; it will consume events from registry SNS topic and mutate the registry routing table via admin API.
- Smoke-runner is a small Lambda-like job (runner/quick-smoke) that runs a pre-defined prompt set; results stored in metrics DB under tag "onboard-smoke".

comments: 2025-02-18 - Ava Chen: Initial triage. Confirmed scope with PM. Drafted acceptance criteria and selected non-blocking attestation option to avoid slowing onboarding velocity.
2025-02-21 - Marcus Rivera: Spike completed for KMS adapter. Found legacy registry schema needs a small change to store 'provisional' state. Created prototype PR #4412.

2025-02-25 - SRE (Jamal Ortiz): Noted that the rollback signal should come from both application errors and infra (OOMs). Suggested adding a circuit-breaker on rollout controller to prevent rapid toggling.
2025-02-27 - Design review (Priya Nair): UX copy for 'provisional' artifacts and attestation states approved. Added tooltip language for console.
2025-03-01 - QA (Liu Wang): Smoke-runner flaked on quantized Llama-7B due to missing env var in runner image. Added a fix and re-ran; results stable.
2025-03-03 - Marcus Rivera: Integrated smoke-runner and added dashboard panels for on-board canaries. Next: formal load test and schedule security review with Compliance.
2025-03-03 - Ava Chen: Added dependency on ENG-18425 for artifact provenance gating policy. Created follow-up ENG-21800 to add customer-managed KMS flow.
notes: Rolling promotion policy: default 5% for 6 hours -> 25% for 12 hours -> 100% if no alerts.
Rollback triggers: >3% regression in eval accuracy on smoke-suite OR P90 latency increase >20% vs baseline.
We will expose attestation fingerprints in the Console artifact detail page under 'Provenance'.
